Arsenal are keeping a close eye on Inter Milan striker Pio Esposito as Mikel Arteta continues to assess potential long-term additions to his attack.

The 21-year-old has emerged as one of Serie A’s most exciting young forwards after an outstanding run for both club and country.

Arsenal have already made enquiries over his availability, but Inter’s response suggests prising him away from San Siro will be extremely difficult.

According to transfer journalist Nicolò Schira, Inter have rejected approaches from Arsenal for Esposito and also turned down an offer worth around €60million from Newcastle United.

The Italian giants consider their academy graduate non-transferable and recently extended his contract until 2032, giving them complete control over his immediate future.

Esposito produced a hat-trick in Inter’s dramatic 4-4 draw with Atalanta on Sunday and has also carried his club form onto the international stage. He scored twice against France on November 12 before finding the net again during Italy’s latest Nations League fixtures.

A fresh report covering Arsenal’s pursuit also confirms that Inter have effectively closed the door on a January deal despite growing Premier League interest.

Esposito certainly fits the profile Arsenal should be targeting.

At 21, he already possesses the physical presence of a traditional No.9 while showing impressive movement, finishing and link-up play. He could eventually give Arteta a long-term focal point rather than another short-term solution.

The problem is Inter’s negotiating position.

A €60m offer has already failed, and with a contract running until 2032 there is absolutely no pressure to sell. Arsenal would probably need to go considerably higher simply to start serious discussions.

That would be difficult to justify in January. Arsenal already have Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres available centrally, so they do not need to turn admiration into an expensive panic move.

The smarter strategy is to continue monitoring Esposito and revisit the situation if Inter’s stance changes.

He looks capable of becoming one of Europe’s leading strikers, but Arsenal should pursue that potential with patience rather than allowing Newcastle’s failed €60m bid to start an unnecessary bidding war.

#1279. The Review: Hibs thought they had turned the corner, but they've gone straight down another cul-de-sac

Published: 15:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 22 November 2026

Just when they thought they were beginning to make some progress, along comes another embarrassing setback for Hibs and the decision-makers who have led them into this most trying of seasons.

Before the international break, the impression was that their recently-appointed head coach Marink Reedijk had turned a corner with that Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden and a 4-0 win at Pittodrie.

Well, if he did, it has taken them headlong into another cul-de-sac. That’s how it felt at Easter Road yesterday when they were trounced 4-0 by Dundee United and left second-bottom of the Premiership table with more than a third of the season completed.

It made rather a mockery of the club’s social media channels, the profile pages of which proudly trumpet their newfound status as ‘Premier Sports Cup finalists’… with an exclamation mark and a golden trophy emoji thrown in for good measure.

Self-respecting Hibs fans won’t be fooled by the propaganda. Not after a humiliating afternoon on which their much-vaunted anthem, ’Sunshine on Leith’, was belted out by a gleeful away support at Easter Road.

Long before Zac Sapsford’s first-half double and strikes after the interval by Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall, some supporters were digging out their anti-board banners and using a megaphone to voice their frustration with those upstairs.

Malky Mackay is under growing pressure from supporters in his role as Hibs sporting director

Zac Sapsford scores the first of Dundee United 's four goals against Hibs at Easter Road

Dundee boss Steven Pressley says that he alone was to blame for their 8-0 thrashing by Hearts

This is how it works at struggling clubs, where fans need someone to blame. First, they target players. Then they single out the manager. When his replacement proves to be no more effective, they have little option but to turn their guns on the board.

Not that there’s anything wrong with holding the hierarchy to account if they are the common denominator in a lengthy period of under-achievement. There has been little sign of progress at Easter Road since Bournemouth owner Bill Foley sold his Hibs shares back to the Gordon family last year, having suggested that they didn’t listen to his input. Big questions are also being asked of sporting director Malky Mackay who was asked in 2024 to lead and oversee the entire football operation, including recruitment and the appointment of a head coach.

Club legend David Gray had his moments as manager, but in the end, supporters wanted rid. Reedijk may turn out to be the real deal but the early signs are that he is struggling with the squad he has inherited. Too many of them failed to do the basics yesterday.

Unlike Hibs, Jim Goodwin’s Dundee United are a strong side with a clear identity. Not for nothing have they gone eight games without defeat, but they scored all too easily as they racked up their biggest-ever victory at Easter Road.

Hibs’ squad appears to be weak, imbalanced and too full of ill-advised signings for Reedijk to make the kind of impact he would like. The holes in it are such that he recently opted to use Scotland defender Grant Hanley as an emergency centre-forward.

Reedijk needs to begin an overhaul of that playing staff in the January window, but how much power will be granted in that process? The Dutch coach has already hinted that he will not be given the final say when it comes to transfers.

The fans are nervous about another rebuild under Mackay and his recruitment staff, whose work in the summer window left a lot to be desired. Jason Kerr was a double-winner with St Johnstone, but he has cut a hapless figure at the back. Midfielder Azeem Abdulai, signed on a three-year contract from Leyton Orient, has made only four appearances, just one from the start. And then there is striker Nathan Lowe, on loan from Stoke City, who is struggling to adapt.

Mackay’s record is under heavy scrutiny. He is to be commended for making a profit of around £6million on striker Kieron Bowie, but why has there been no substantial replacement since the striker’s move to Italy nearly a year ago? Can he really argue that expensive signings such as Thibault Klidje and Ante Suto have been value for money?

A club of Hibs’ size, with those resources, should not be in the relegation zone. Nor should they be struggling so pitifully in their own stadium – they have lost nine of their last ten league games there and haven’t taken three points at home since April.

Which tees up nicely Dundee’s visit to Easter Road on Tuesday, not least because the Tayside club suffered a humiliation of their own this weekend. While Hibs were conceding four, Steven Pressley's side were shipping eight in a hammering by Hearts that has surely inflicted significant psychological damage.

To his great credit, Pressley insisted afterwards that he alone was to blame for his team’s wretched performance. That may have been true on the night, but over an extended period, a club’s fortunes tend to be shaped by decisions off the pitch. As Hibs have been finding out.

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee is reportedly being eyed by Como after the Serie A side were dealt a devastating injury blow to Moise Kean.

The Dutchman has made 11 appearances for the Red Devils so far this season but every one of those has come as a substitute, with his 45 minutes off the bench at Anfield on Sunday the longest runout he’s had in the current campaign (Transfermarkt).

He turned down the opportunity to join Fiorentina during the summer transfer window, but rumours over a potential return to Italy for the ex-Bologna marksman refuse to go away.

According to Gianluca di Marzio, Como are interested in Zirkzee as a potential centre-forward acquisition for the January transfer window as they seek attacking reinforcements after Kean aggravated an existing injury, thus ruling out for an extended period.

The report adds that the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick’s successor is ‘another variable to consider’ as to whether the new boss will green-light an exit for the Nerherlands forward.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Even with Benjamin Sesko sidelined, Zirkzee has struggled to get much of a look-in for United so far this season, but perhaps Pochettino might be more willing to give him a fair crack than Carrick had been.

Despite him playing just 231 minutes in the current campaign, only three teammates have scored more than the Dutchman’s two goals, and he has the best goals-per-minute ratio of anyone to have found the net for the Red Devils in 2026/27 (Transfermarkt).

One of those strikes came in the form of a stoppage-time consolation against Como last month, with that 4-1 victory for Cesc Fabregas’ side helping the Champions League debutants to the lofty heights of fourth in the table at the midway point of the league phase.

Gaz Drinkwater of BBC Radio Manchester‘s The Devils’ Advocate podcast described the 25-year-old as ‘slick’ on the ball, but also lacking the pace required to succeed in the Premier League, with a record of only six goals in 63 English top-flight games.

How much game-time Zirkzee is handed between now and the end of December will tell a lot as to how highly Pochettino regards him. The latest dugout change at Old Trafford might afford the number 11 a new lease of life; conversely, it could push him towards the exit door if he continues to be left feeding off scraps.

Once again, the 25-year-old’s future is set to be a pertinent talking point in the run-up to a transfer window.

#1277. THE END GAME? Writing is on the wall for McCann after revitalised Dons ran riot at Rugby Park

Published: 18:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 22 November 2026

Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.

Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.

The writing already appears to be on the wall for the 52-year-old. A question of when, rather than if, he is given his jotters.

By all accounts, he hasn’t lost the dressing room. Which is just as well, because he has well and truly lost the punters, whose collective mood shifted from angry to apathetic over the course of 90-odd thoroughly entertaining minutes at Rugby Park on Saturday.

McCann knows this himself. It is not as if he is operating with the blinkers on.

It's a tough watch for Neil McCann as his Kilmarnock team go down 4-2 to Aberdeen

His assessment of his team’s performances week-to-week tends to be pretty honest, as it was again this weekend.

The problem is, as he put it, that he is coming across ‘like a broken record’.

His team are hopeless at the back and toothless up top, with some encouraging stuff in between. If the supporters are sick of hearing it, imagine how scunnered McCann must feel saying it. He certainly looks it.

If they continue to defend like this, relegation is a nailed-on certainty.

They shipped four here — and it could have very easily been a few more — to take their tally to 33 conceded for the season in just 14 games. It’s laughable, there’s no other way to dress it up.

Aberdeen’s Kevin Nisbet scored twice in four first-half minutes, capitalising on a woeful clearance from keeper Nico Mantl to put the Dons ahead, before curling a free-kick straight through the weakest wall you’ve ever seen in your life to double the visitors’ advantage.

New Dons boss Mario Frick can't hide his delight after victory in first game in charge

The third goal — shortly after Greg Kiltie had given McCann’s men a lifeline — was the worst of the lot. Former Rugby Park skipper Brad Lyons ghosted in behind the completely unaware Michael Schjonning-Larsen to head the ball home after Cathal McCarthy failed to stop Nesta Guinness-Walker’s cross from the left touchline.

Shocking stuff all round, and exactly the type of goal which has killed Killie all season — and will continue to do so until something drastic changes.

Let’s not forget, the recent international break afforded McCann and his staff a fortnight to work on things on the training pitch ahead of what is going to be a gruelling winter schedule.

While the Killie manager will ultimately be the one to pay the price, his players need to have a right good look at themselves too. There was simply no sign of anyone in that backline taking any sort of responsibility.

Kilmarnock’s next three games are against St Mirren, Hibernian and Motherwell — the three sides currently directly above them in the table.

An absolute minimum of four points from that run is required, otherwise this is going to get rather ugly. In truth, defeat in Paisley this weekend may well be the final nail in McCann’s coffin.

On the other hand, things are finally starting to look up for the Dons.

New manager Mario Frick has promised to bring heavy metal football to these shores, and if Saturday is anything to go by, the ex-Liechtenstein international is a man of his word.

McCann's job looks to be on the line after bottom club Killie succumbed to another defeat

His team were a joy to watch going forward here, particularly in the first half.

It was a million miles away from the kind of turgid football offered up under his predecessor as Dons manager, Stephen Robinson.

Speed, intensity, aggression, quality. The performance was full of it.

You could count the number of times the Dons faffed about with the ball on one hand. Every time there was an opportunity to get forward, they took it.

Ante Palaversa, making his first appearance of the campaign, was at the heart of it.

For whatever reason, Robinson never fancied the Croatian, a stance which perplexed the Pittodrie faithful. Indeed, the 26-year-old — once on the books of Manchester City — was deemed surplus to requirements over the summer.

The Dons will be delighted there were no takers.

He was outstanding here as he commanded that space between midfield and defence without breaking sweat. Nobody in Killie colours could get near him.

Both Nicky Devlin and Guinness-Walker bombed up their respective wings all day, while some of the link-up play between Nisbet — who should have had a hat-trick before Findlay Marshall wrapped things up late on — and Hicham Mahou was delightful.

Defensively, they were all over the shop at times, and no doubt they will be punished heavily at Ibrox on Tuesday night if they are as open as this.

But this was a display to simply be enjoyed rather than picked apart. It makes a change.

KILMARNOCK (4-2-3-1): Mantl 3; McCarthy 4, Kamson-Kamara 3 (Brandon 46), Stanger 4, Schjonning-Larsen 4; Lowery 6, Tshibola 5 (McKenzie 85); Ring 3 (O’Hara 46), Kiltie 6 (Clescenco 83), Hugill 5.5; Owen 4 (John-Jules 54). Booked: Owen, Hugill. Manager: Neil McCann 3.

ABERDEEN (4-1-3-2): Muller 5; Devlin 6, Molloy 6, Milne 6, Guinness- Walker 7; PALAVERSA 8 (Aremu 61); Lyons 7, Briedl 7 (Mouloula 61), Armstrong 6.5 (Marshall 71); Mahou 6 (Smith 80), Nisbet 8. Booked: None. Manager: Mario Frick 7.

#1276. People entering old age now have better memory than their parents did

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty

People born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November. The analysis offers clues about why dementia rates have fallen by 13% per decade over the past 27 years in Europe and the United States2.

The researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words. The study included 219,000 people aged 50 and older who were born between 1910 and 1964, and tracked changes in their scores over three decades. These list-based tests are commonly used to screen for dementia and Alzheimer’s disease.

Consistent with previous studies3, people born more recently entered old age with better memory performance compared with those born in earlier generations. A ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Memory decline also seems to have become less steep across successive generations, says study co-author Anders Fjell, a neuropsychologist at the University of Oslo in Norway.

The findings are “confirmatory” of other studies on the topic, which indicated that the rate of memory decline is slowing down but weren’t statistically significant, says Carol Brayne, an epidemiologist who studies dementia at the University of Cambridge, UK. “It is another piece of the jigsaw.”

Because many populations around the world are ageing — that is, older individuals are becoming a larger proportion of the total population — the number of people living with dementia is increasing worldwide. But an individual person’s risk of dementia at any given age has dropped by two-thirds over the past 40 years in the United States4. “For those who reach 80, a smaller percentage [of people] will get dementia than before,” explains Fjell.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active

To understand what might be driving this trend, Fjell and his colleagues used longitudinal data on individuals’ cognitive performance to estimate their memory trajectories over time. The authors examined whether people born later in the twentieth century showed differences in their memory performance and their rate of memory decline compared with those born earlier.

The analysis found that with each successive birth decade, people were 64% more likely to maintain stable memory function — that is, experience little or no memory deterioration.

The authors also investigated brain imaging data from nearly 2,000 people over a median of four years. They found that a stable memory during ageing also corresponded to a decrease in shrinkage of the hippocampus — a brain region involved in memory formation.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03783-9

#1275. Mauricio Pochettino was immediately up against it in his first few days at this slow-motion car crash of a club - Man United's 4-0 loss at Liverpool showed how much he has to do: OLIVER HOLT

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

That was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this misused, abused, diminished, fallen slow-motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

And then Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

So at least Pochettino got to see United set a new record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done more quickly by United in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to watch it through your fingers. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder and more and more pale in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his big coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars

And in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the esteemed actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

And the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

So, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

This is a relegation fight that United are in. Don’t kid yourself that it’s not. The last time they dropped out of the top flight in 1973-74, they won three games in their first 11 matches. This season, they have won just once in the first 11 and that was at home to Ipswich Town on August 30th. A lot of the teams around them have got something about them, too. They certainly have more spirit than this rabble.

In that context, it was not the best omen that this was the worst result in a United manager’s first game for more than 100 years. If Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a big ask, rebuilding United is up there with it. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

It was strange seeing a new United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

It was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

It did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise

Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85)

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46)

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey

Three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

United were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

And so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

There was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

That feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

Manchester United have stepped up their pursuit of Borussia Dortmund youngster Mathis Albert, with Mauricio Pochettino keen to reunite the talented winger with the club at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils are reportedly among the clubs intensifying their efforts to secure the 17-year-old’s signature, as Barcelona also look to strengthen their position in the race for the highly-rated American prospect.

According to a report from TEAMtalk, both clubs have made fresh enquiries in recent weeks, with Albert attracting growing interest from some of Europe’s biggest sides. The teenager joined Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has quickly become one of the Bundesliga’s most promising young players.

Albert made history in April 2026, becoming the youngest American to feature in the Bundesliga, coming off the bench during Dortmund’s 4-0 victory over Freiburg. His impressive development has also earned him senior international recognition, having scored for the United States under Pochettino.

The winger has, however, struggled to secure regular first-team opportunities under Niko Kovac this season, with most of his appearances coming from the bench. His limited involvement could potentially open the door to a move elsewhere, although Dortmund remain determined to retain his services.

Pochettino is understood to be a major admirer of Albert, having handed him his international debut and closely followed his development. The Argentine manager could now look to bring the youngster to Manchester as he continues shaping his squad.

Albert previously rejected approaches from Manchester City, Barcelona and Bayern Munich to remain in Germany, while Chelsea, Arsenal, Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain have also monitored his situation.

Dortmund are reportedly unwilling to part ways with the teenager and have already offered him a contract extension, with his current deal expiring in June 2027.

A potential transfer is unlikely to materialise before next summer, when Albert turns 18 in May. United could face significant competition, but Pochettino’s connection with the player may prove an important factor in their pursuit.

#1273. Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a big moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”

Forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to quickly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner said: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

“It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”

We knew the margins would be really small. They are extremely well coached and organised. The longer the game goes on they gain more belief. We had to be so patient - and clinical when we got the chance. The way they were defending, they were more comfortable. But we have players with different qualities and can adapt to what the game is delivering.

We have another three big chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating them, they will come.

Let’s enjoy the win, because it was a very tough one. And then, on Wednesday, we have an incredible game against Bayern Munich away [in the Champions League].

When you see their goal it’s deflected otherwise, it’s straight to the gloves of Matz Sels. You have periods in football where you feel everything going against you and then there are periods when things are on your side.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good.

Noni [Madueke], Jurrien [Timber], Mikel [Merino] was brilliant when he came on and Viktor [Gyokeres] really changed the game - all of them did and that’s what we need. Noni obviously the highlight because he scored the goal and that’s the difference.

Sometimes you can get frustrated with teams who are difficult to break down. First half we didn’t have a shot on target and that’s something we discussed. We had another two big ones in the second half but the only one on target we had was a little deflection and it’s in.

Great reaction [after scoring goal], to have the will to defend a really open and difficult and stressful situation.

We knew it would be a tough game, it always is against Arsenal. They have a good team. But we feel we can change the result, maybe a draw, maybe a win. Now we have to put it in the past and focus on the next match.

We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas. We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best.

If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd so we know that we’re going to start some and finish some and for me it’s the same mentality every time I just want to create or score.

Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.

We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.

32 - Since Mikel Arteta became Arsenal manager in December 2019, they have had the joint-most 1-0 wins in the Premier League of any side (32, level with Everton). Stereotype. https://t.co/nD7C3j7Xjw

Arsenal dig out a very ugly victory, and one they probably did not warrant. Forest can take positives from their performance, primarily the solidity of their defending and a more threatening Delap performance.

Forest with another late moment of danger! Delap peeled in behind the Arsenal defence, and he was found by a glorious pass, but Konsa made a fantastic last-ditch challenge to surely preserve the points from Arsenal.

What a goal that would have been from Murillo! The burly defender did so well to skip between Konsa and Saka, before sending Rice the wrong way in the box with a roll of the studs. Murillo tired for the curler into the top corner with his weaker right foot, and he was not far away. Great effort.

Forest cling on by their fingernails with Arsenal flooding forward, but Merino’s pass to Saka in the box was underhit. Chris Wood and Hudson-Odoi are now on for Forest as they chase an equaliser. Cunha and McAtee the Forest players to depart.

Odegaard with a week free-kick from a good crossing position after Saka won a foul, before Raya’s long ball towards Gyokeres is too strong and Forest have a goal kick. Arsenal still to muster a shot on target from 73 per cent possession.

Ndoye are Dominguez are the Forest players coming off in a double change, replaced by Kalimuendo and Sangare. Forest will be worth a point if the game continues this way.

Declan Rice with a shank out for a throw when he was looking for Saka. Kalimuendo is ready to come for Forest, so Glasner is introducing another forward.

Good chance for Rice but he blasts over! Arsenal’s best move of the game with Saka, Odegaard and Timber working as a triangle to get in behind the Forest defence, and Timber’s pull-back was accurate. Rice was always leaning back though as he tried to sweep the ball into the far corner.

Delap with a tame shot from distance, before Timber instigates a more dangerous Arsenal attack with a reverse pass into Odegaard. The ball is worked to Madueke and his deflected cross is headed away. Arsenal building some pressure, and they have another corner. Arteta signalling that he wants to make the change before the corner is taken and here come the changes: White for Timber, Havertz for Gyokeres and Merino on for Bruno Guimaraes.

Gabriel meets Rice’s delivery, but he fails to direct his header on target.

Saka and Rice lose duels when fishing for fouls and Forest have another corner. Arsenal’s performance level has certainly not improved since half-time.

The first half was an attack against defence session for long periods but Arsenal know they are in an arm wrestle now. Forest far more aggressive, and the crowd are more involved. But that could open up avenues of space. White with a really poor pass towards Saka which is astray.

Arsenal have a corner of their own after breaking from Raya’s gloves. Much more open game so far.

Forest deal with Saka’s delivery, and there was a very brief VAR check for a handball penalty. Nothing doing.

Madueke looking dangerous, receiving a Gabriel ball over the top and dashing inside but his shot was blocked.

Delap’s shot from a tight angle is then deflected wide. Forest corner, from which Murillo’s header loops into Raya’s gloves. Forest showing more attacking ambition.

Liam Delap is producing a very decent centre-forward performance.

Madueke and Rice not one the same wavelength, before Delap does well to win a shoulder to shoulder with Gabriel only to slice his cross behind for an Arsenal goal kick. Sums up the lack of attacking quality in the game.

Forest have another free-kick in a shooting position after Havertz is penalised for blocking a long shot with his hand. McAtee’s effort from the free-kick is scooped miles over the bar.

Both teams looking livelier in the early exchanges of the half, but Forest’s counter-attack was the more dangerous, with Liam Delap doing well to hold on to the ball and whipping a cross into the box that was just ahead of Williams.

Noni Madueke replaces Eberechi Eze, so a more natural wide player on his stronger foot on Arsenal’s left flank.

Frustrating first half for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta will be demanding more from his attacking players.

Arsenal have not registered a shot on target so far and their delivery from set-pieces has been poor.

Forest look relatively comfortable and had the best chance of the half with a shot from Dan Ndoye which was saved by David Raya.

Are we heading for a hat-trick of 0-0 draws at the City Ground between these two teams?

A very uneventful 45 minutes which has been played at the pace of a pre-season game at times. Similarities with the last two fixtures between these teams at the City Ground, and Arsenal’s games against Leeds and Lille this week. They put their foot on the pedal after half-time in both games, and they need to do the same here.

Guimaraes is off the pitch, and there will be more than two minutes added now as a result of his treatment. Forest win a corner, but Havertz heads away at the near post.

Just the two minutes of added time to play.

Liam Delap wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Forest after Arsenal were caught with numbers forward. Big moment for the home team, this. Calafiori was caught on the ball again, he has not had the best of games.

Williams and McAtee are over the free keek, which is around 25 yards out, left of centre.

Williams blasts the ball into Bruno Guimaraes, who goes down and stays down after taking the shot flush in the face.

More incisive from Arsenal, with Rice punching the ball into Odegaard and then on to Havertz but the angle was always against him and the German could only shoot into the side-netting. Forest have defended very well, overall. Although they have been deep for the most part, they have jumped and pushed out at the right times to stop Arsenal accessing the box.

Glasner and Arteta dish out some instruction while there is a stoppage in play to deal with a hand in the face that troubled Schlager. Can either side find a breakthrough before the break?

David Raya claimed that Forest corner with ease and the game has now resumed its pattern. Forest retreating into their shape, and Arsenal passing in front of them. Schlager penalised for a foul on Saka, the home fans not happy with the decision, I think because Saka was going away from goal.

Rice clips in a menacing delivery, but Havertz skewed his header wide from seven or eight yards. Good chance, Arsenal’s best so far.

More Arsenal probing but the small details are letting them down: Eze’s return to Odegaard forced his team-mate to check, and then Odegaard’s touch was heavy after a wall pass from Guimaraes.

Delap does well to make a nuisance of himself at the other end, and his long-range shot deflects behind for a corner.

Strong from Konsa to win the ball, drive out of defence and win a foul. Rice with a well-weighted scoop over the Forest defence for the run of Ben White, but he skewed his cross behind for a goal kick.

Arsenal with another corner. No doubt they have been the game’s dominant force when it comes to possession and territory, but there has been a lack of cutting edge so far. Saka goes for the near post again but Forest deal with it. The home crowd groan at Sels for not releasing the ball quickly in search of a break.

Arsenal work the ball across their midfield with Guimaraes, Rice and Odegaard all involved, and a dangerous Saka cross is headed behind for a corner.

Scramble! The near-post flick on caused chaos and Konsa’s goal-bound backheel was blocked, but the ball would not quite drop for Ben White to score a tap-in.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

It’s a very tight affair with Arsenal enjoying more of the possession but Forest seemingly happy with that and content to them on the break.

Bruno Guimaraes has made a bright start for the visitors.

Forest’s best attacking moment of the game and it comes from an Arsenal mistake.

Calafiori just had to play a five-yard pass back to Gabriel but scuffed it, and Munoz pounced. Running at the Arsenal penalty area, Munoz’s cross was deflected to the back post and the ball found it’s way to Ndoye. Decent reverse shot through legs, but Raya had it covered and tipped around the post.

From the corner, Forest are penalised for a foul.

Arsenal continue to have Forest penned in their own half, very difficult for the home team to play through the midfield or over Konsa and Gabriel so far.

Saka produces his first successful dribble to beat Williams, and the left wing-back trips him at the expense of a free-kick and a booking. Rice’s delivery from the right was uncharacteristically poor.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

It’s already pretty clear that one of the key duels today will be between Gabriel and Liam Delap.

Forest’s record signing Delap has already let Gabriel know he’s in the game with his physicality.

Cute pass from Bruno Guimaraes to break the Forest midfield line and find Odegaard, but strangely the Arsenal captain could not sort his feet out to control the ball and back a clean pass. Then Williams defends well against Saka from an Arsenal attacking transition.

Pretty subdued start from Forest. The crowd’s spirits were raised there by Delap chasing down Konsa who had the deal with the sun his eyes, but the Forest striker pushed him in the back.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

Arsenal get the game under way, and play short from kick-off.

There will be a degree of pressure on birthday boy James McAtee today to make an impression.

With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, McAtee is likely to take the No 10 position and continue his redemption arc.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.

Fascinating stuff from Sam Dean this morning, who has profiled a member of Mikel Arteta’s inner circle who is not listed on Arsenal’s website. Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Things started with a phone call with Nicolas Jover, then a meeting with Arteta and now he splits his time between Argentina and London. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

#1270. Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026

When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.

It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.

Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied.

With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional big guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about.

But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way.

Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off.

Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton

McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May.

Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic said of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very important for us.'

Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler said: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team.

'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today showed there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.'

Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table

Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility.

The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork.

At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly.

Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis.

That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed.

Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts.

As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar.

The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time.

Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar.

Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out

As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull showed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards.

Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining.

The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move.

Moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands.

McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves.

'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!'

Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August.

Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team

Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches.

Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so important,' declared Jakirovic.

'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.'

#1268. Leeds United Can Convince Celtic to Sell 'Best Striker' Durán with Right Offer

Leeds United may be able to tempt a cash-hungry Celtic board into selling a prize asset if they are willing to spend a significant chunk. The Whites are said to be interested in Celtic frontman Camilo Durán, who has dazzled since joining the Scottish club in the summer.

Durán joined the Hoops for a bargain £5.5million deal from Qarabag after netting five times in the Champions League last season, and he has hit the ground running. The forward has scored 14 goals across all competitions, and he has found the net just as regularly in the Europa League as in the Scottish Premiership.

He has even been a consistent scorer when starting on the right wing, where he has often found himself to make room for centre-forward Kasper Hogh, who arrived on an £11million deal but has only scored three times and is now more than three months without a goal.

And don't be fooled by Celtic's competition. The Hoops signed right-winger Haissem Hassan for £6million - which could raise to £9million - during the summer window, with the Egypt international having impressed during the World Cup, but he is without a goal up to this point, so even other higher quality players are not having the success in front of goal from the same positions Durán is operating in. And that's a big part of the reason clubs like Leeds are said to be scouting the Colombian.

But Celtic's reliance on Durán means it's going to be hard to lure the Colombian away from Parkhead, especially during the season. A January deal is going to be particularly difficult to strike, although there may be a slither of hope if Celtic are eliminated from the Europa League before then. The Bhoys currently have three points after four games and will need six or seven points from their last four to extend their European campaign.

That could be a key factor, but in any case, a summer deal remains realistic if Leeds are willing to pay north of £15million, which would give Celtic the chance of tripling their £5.5million investment in the space of just one year.

"I believe he is the future of Colombian football and he should be first pick in our team. For me, he is the best striker we have." - Arnulfo Valentierra (Durán's former Independiente Medellín manager) speaking this season.

This Celtic board has previously turned down big money in the January window, blocking the £25million exit of Arne Engels last January, but they sold him for £3million less in the summer when West Ham came calling. They never replaced the midfielder, either, leaving fans furious amid an ongoing civil war between them and the board over a perceived lack of ambition.

“We are building a team here and guys like Camilo are part of the future. He has a lot of talent.” - Nestor Lorenzo (Colombia head coach)

This Celtic board likes to turn a profit, and it is willing to do it at the cost of the team to a certain degree. Another sale could complicate things, and Benjamin Nygren is the leading candidate to leave next summer as things stand, but if Leeds can get in early and make a sizable offer for Durán, the bargain deal he arrived at Celtic on will give them a chance of sealing a deal, as long as they are willing to stump up a sizable amount of cash compared to that initial £5.5million fee.

Camilo Duran has been in electric form for Celtic and Leeds United have been scouting the 14-goal man this season

#1266. £35m Star's Man Utd Career is Already Over After Pochettino's First Match

Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of Manchester United couldn't have gone any worse, and the writing is already on the wall for a number of players following the Argentine's first 90 minutes in the dugout as he sets about trying to revolutionise Man United.

Pochettino arrived in Manchester last week knowing that a point would probably be enough to take the club out of the Premier League's relegation zone, and he set up his team to get at least that when they face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

However, his game plan was ripped up eight minutes into the match when Leny Yoro was red-carded after being adjudged to have brought down Alexander Isak as the last man outside the penalty area.

If Pochettino wasn't fully aware of his side's defensive shortcomings before taking over, he is now, and the club now have the worst defensive record out of every club in Europe's top five European leagues.

Luke Shaw wasn't even involved on Merseyside, but he might now be undroppable after what the former Spurs boss witnessed against Andoni Iraola's men, as Diogo Dalot once again struggled out of position at left-back.

Yoro continues to flatter to deceive following a big-money move from Lille, while Matthijs de Ligt and Lisandro Martinez both endured nightmare afternoons against Liverpool.

The latter seems likely to leave Old Trafford in 2027 given his contract expires at the end of the season, and given he publicly spoke out against Jason Wilcox's recruitment following the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid last month.

The Argentina international was fined and given a 'dressing down' by Wilcox, according to one report, and it's difficult to see why they would want to keep him around beyond next summer.

Martinez isn't the only United player whose Old Trafford career could be over though, especially when you consider Joshua Zirkzee's situation.

There was excitement when United signed Joshua Zirkzee from Bologna for £35m in 2024, given his level of performance for the Serie A outfit and the fact that he had shown he was a player capable of the spectacular.

However, the Netherlands international quickly lost the manager who signed him, Erik ten Hag, when he was sacked in October 2024, and has failed to convince Ruben Amorim or Michael Carrick since that he was worthy of regular minutes on the pitch.

Even in the absence of the injured Benjamin Sesko in recent months, when Carrick had no other recognised striker to turn to, Zirkzee was still often left on the substitutes' bench.

Now, the Times have reported that, despite their defensive issues, United have prioritised signing a new striker in January, such is their concerns about how things have gone without Sesko.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is keen to be reunited with Pochettino having worked with him during the duo's time with the United States national team.

With Sesko also due back from his shin injury in January or February, Zirkzee will be left as the third-choice option if he remains at Old Trafford beyond January.

The 25-year-old may have been given 45 minutes at Anfield on Sunday, but he failed to make much of an impact, albeit in difficult circumstances after his side were reduced to 10 men so early in the game.

Given how things have gone this season for Zirkzee, coupled with his limited minutes under the previous two managers, the fact that United are prioritising a new striker over defenders tells you all you need to know - his United career is over.

#1265. Ange Postecoglou snaps at reporter as he defends Sadio Mane for missing match to be at birth of child - after defeat which saw Cristiano Ronaldo fail to score a penalty

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child

'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most important thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

'(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more important in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

#1264. Rio Ngumoha dazzles on coming-of-age night in Europe

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

This young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

Ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. A very interesting team selection from Andoni Iraola. Liverpool’s head coach had indicated at his pre-match press conference that he was going to go as strong as possible, as his side seek to secure their third straight Champions League win. But the very fact Iraola has chosen to put Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola on the bench indicates he has one eye on Sunday’s demanding assignment against Brighton at Anfield.

Iraola will be delighted to have Cody Gakpo fit again and Lewis Koumas certainly deserves another opportunity to lead the line. But after victory’s against Atletico Madrid and LASK, Liverpool have given themselves some breathing space and it is understandable if Iraola, who has bemoaned the lack of time he has to train his squad, is already plotting Brighton’s downfall.

Your Reds to take on Villarreal in the #UCL! 🔴💫 https://t.co/tlQNFZVMBv

The club known as the “Yellow Submarine” made themselves some fans in the red half of Merseyside by denying Everton a place in the Champions League proper in 2005/06. Everton lost 4-2 on aggregate, and there was controversy in the second leg in Spain when Pierluigi Collina disallowed a Duncan Ferguson header that could have taken the tie to extra time. Everton had finished fourth, one place above Liverpool, the previous season, but Liverpool’s triumph in Istanbul assured them of a qualification place too. Unlike Everton, they prevailed.

Speaking of which, Rafael Benitez is at Anfield this evening.

Dominic King takes stock of Andoni Iraola’s first 10 games in charge of Liverpool and, despite some teething problems, he believes there are reasons to be optimistic. The demands Iraola is putting on Liverpool’s midfielders are an interesting tactical wrinkle, with Dom writing: “Liverpool’s formation will always be written as 4-2-3-1, but the reality is that Iraola’s team do not play in four clear tactical lines. He asks specific jobs of his midfielders, deploying them detailed instructions, and it is going to require some patience before performances become consistent.”

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

They have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

Iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

#1263. Tottenham Offered Chance To Sign Ivan Toney, De Zerbi Needs Him

After signing 10 new players in the summer across all areas of the pitch, you would think that Tottenham Hotspur's squad is in a strong state.

It would be fair to say that there is good depth across the defence and midfield in particular, with Marcos Senesi and Luca Williams-Barnett coming into the starting XI against Ipswich Town on Saturday and producing performances that make them undroppable against Sunderland next time out.

Tottenham have now won three successive Premier League matches for the first time in nearly two years, and they are now in the top half of the table having been rock-bottom earlier in the season.

Spurs are certainly improving but there is still a way to go to get to where they want to be under Roberto De Zerbi, who signed a long-term contract to build a project at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

While the north London outfit have looked strong defensively in recent matches, conceding 11 in 11 top flight matches this term, their goalscoring is more of a concern.

Saturday's double against the Tractor Boys took their tally to 12 in 11, but they need to be better than that if they want to really push on and be in contention for a European spot this term.

De Zerbi has had a striker conundrum all season, having begun the campaign with Richarlison in the centre-forward position, even though the Brazilian had informed during the summer that he wanted to leave the club.

After failing to secure a move away from Spurs, the former Everton attacker remains exiled and on the sidelines, while Dominic Solanke continues to fail to show that he is the consistent goalscorer needed.

De Zerbi has used Omar Marmoush in the striker role too, following his summer move from Manchester City, but the Egyptian international has also failed to fire there, and it's difficult to see exactly where he fits in.

It's becoming apparent that the Italian boss needs extra competition for Solanke, and TEAMtalk report that they have been contacted about the potential availability of Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney by intermediaries.

If De Zerbi wants a striker who has proven he can put the ball in the back of the net regularly in January, there might not be many better options than the England international.

The report claims that the 30-year-old is weighing up a return to England in the New Year, with intermediaries proposing a loan move featuring an option to buy, if Al-Ahli would be willing to agree to that.

A number of Premier League clubs are said to have been contacted by those intermediaries, including Tottenham, Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United.

New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank is also keen to be reunited with Toney having worked with him at Brentford previously, and that would probably be the landing spot where he'd be guaranteed the most minutes.

Even though Toney has moved to Saudi Arabia, he has continued to be prolific and he has 16 goals in 17 appearances for Al-Ahli this term.

Such has been his form in Saudi that former Al-Ahli sporting director Rui Pedro labelled him 'one of the best strikers in the world', while his England teammate Declan Rice has also been full of praise for him in the past.

Toney's England call-ups followed on from his performances and numbers for Brentford, and his goalscoring form has continued ever since.

He's kind of like Harry Kane in a way where he's not only an out-and-out striker, he's a playmaker as well - his left and right footed passing, the way he picks out his teammates is a special technique to have.

Toney has proven that he can score regularly in the Premier League, and it will be interesting to see who wins the race to bring him back to the Premier League if it's a move that does become possible in the winter market.

Manchester United want to back Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window
